editorial:
If you are looking for a powerful and emotional drama, this one will stay with you long after the credits roll. The story follows Bobby Griffith, a bright and loving young man growing up in a deeply religious family in California. He is his mother's favorite, but he is hiding a secret that eats away at him. When he finally comes out as gay, his mother's reaction is not what he hoped for, and the family is thrown into a painful struggle between faith and love. The movie handles this heavy topic with care and honesty, never feeling preachy or fake. You will feel every moment of Bobby's pain and his family's confusion.

Sigourney Weaver gives an incredible performance as Bobby's mother, Mary. She carries the whole movie on her shoulders and makes you believe every tear and every change of heart. The pacing is steady and builds slowly toward a heartbreaking turn, so be ready for an emotional ride. The only downside is that it can feel a bit heavy at times, and some scenes are tough to watch. Still, it is a must-see for anyone who cares about family, acceptance, and real human stories.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Bobby, overwhelmed by rejection and despair, takes his own life. His death shatters the family, especially his mother Mary. Over time, Mary reads Bobby's diary and begins to understand his pain. She transforms from a strict religious mother into a passionate advocate for LGBTQ+ youth. The movie ends with Mary speaking at a PFLAG meeting, sharing Bobby's story and urging parents to love and accept their children. It is a hopeful but heartbreaking conclusion that turns tragedy into a call for change.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about family, faith, and acceptance.
